Unofficial until approved by the
  Alhambra City Council

  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  February 26, 2024
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:01 p.m., on Monday, February 26, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Stover, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Public Information Specialist, Director of Parks &
Recreation Macias, Director of Library Services LohGuan, Director of Public Works/Utilities Ray,
Director of Finance Lieu, Director of Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho,
Police Chief Kennedy, Fire Chief Ragusa

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maza

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

PRESENTATIONS

1.  LOS ANGELES COMMUNITY COLLEGE DISTRICT: EAST LOS ANGELES COLLEGE
  INFORMATIONAL UPDATE – F2M24-16

  The Los Angeles Community College District (LACCD) is the nation’s largest community
  college district serving over 200,000 students. The district strives to deliver accessible, quality
  education and career opportunities to the students of Los Angeles County. One goal of the
  LACCD was to update cities about the many educational programs and services available to
  their constituents. Residents in Alhambra are served by East Los Angeles College (ELAC),
  which offers university transfer and career education. Dr. Miguel DUEÑAS, Vice President of
  Student Services, Dr. Christina TAFOYA, Vice President of Instructional Services, Michael
  PASCUAL, Vice President of Administrative Services, and Erica MAYORGA, Dean of
  Continuing Education and Workforce Development/South Gate, gave a presentation regarding
  ELAC and the latest information LACCD had to offer. The presentation is on file in the City
  Clerk’s office.

  Public Comment:  Shirley TATSUNO spoke in support of ELAC, her family’s history, the
  services offered during the pandemic through the Foundation, her personal history with the
  college and the Vincent Price Art Museum.

  Discussion:  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER spoke regarding her and her family
  1
2-26-24
   history with ELAC, expressed support for the college, and commended ELAC for their outreach
  during the pandemic.

  Councilmember LEE commended the ELAC representatives for their work and the support
  offered to students.

  Vice Mayor PÉREZ spoke in support of the basic needs support services offered by ELAC for
  their students, and specifically referred to the housing support. Ms. PÉREZ and Dr. DUEÑAS
  further discussed the housing services offered for students and partnership with the City of
  Alhambra. Ms. PÉREZ also suggested partnership with the Alhambra Civic Center Library for
  a variety of programs.

  Mayor MAZA expressed support of ELAC and congratulated them for their work.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed this informational report.

2.  INTRODUCTION OF THE NEW GENERAL SERVICE MANAGER FOR REPUBLIC
  SERVICES – F2M20-39

  Pilar ALMEIDA, Municipal Relationship Manager, with Republic Services introduced New
  General Service Manager for Republic Services JP Robinson and New Area Municipal
  Manager Steven Herring. Mr. ROBINSON and Mr. HERRING provided their personal and
  professional backgrounds and offered continued support for the City of Alhambra.

  Discussion: Council thanked the representatives from Republic Services for their work and
  welcomed them to the team.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed this informational report.

3.  SAN GABRIEL VALLEY COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS TRANSIT FEASIBILITY STUDY –
  F2M24-16

  The San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments (SGVCOG) conducted a Transit Feasibility
  Study for the San Gabriel Valley, in response to the Metro Board's decision in 2020 to withdraw
  the SR 60 alternative for the Eastside Transit Corridor Phase 2 project to extend the Metro E
  Line (formerly the L and Gold). The purpose of the study was to evaluate and enhance mobility
  and improve public transit in the region, with particular focus on serving the communities
  impacted from the project’s withdrawal. Ricky CHOI, Director of Government and Community
  Relations for the SGVCOG, and Roy CHOI, Manager of Transportation, provided a brief
  overview of the study and its status, including a summary of the remaining conceptual
  alternatives and how they benefit east/west and north south travel within the San Gabriel
  Valley through a mix of bus-only bus rapid transit (BRT) lanes and mixed-flow lanes. The
  presentation is on file in the City Clerk’s office. Additionally, SGVCOG staff discussed
  considerations studied for that portion of Valley Blvd. within Alhambra.

  Public Comment:

  1) Xana HERMOSILLO, via Zoom, requested more information regarding the lack of
  dedicated BRT lane on Valley Blvd.

  2) Lewis MCCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., referred to the long-range vision map and
  discussed the potential in-fill station at Atlantic Blvd. He commended Council for approving
  an affordable housing project near that potential site.

  2
2-26-24
   Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER discussed Metro’s decision to support
  the SR 60 freeway, the elimination of a bus line on Valley Blvd., and the importance of
  transportation in the region. Mr. Roy CHOI clarified that the elimination of the bus line on Valley
  Blvd. was due to feedback they received and studies which showed higher ridership on
  Garvey. Mr. Ricky CHOI stated that the Valley segment was included as part of the proposed
  rapid bus priority corridor which would provide other benefits to existing public transit.

  Councilmember LEE and Mr. Roy CHOI discussed the bus fare rates, the estimated trip time
  for the entire route, incentives at the first and last mile to encourage public transit rather than
  personal vehicles, and active transportation projects in the East SGV area to support increased
  bike usage and pedestrian usage. Mr. Roy CHOI continued to discuss changing trends in civic
  planning and development to manage transportation without expanding capacity in an effort to
  move away from a car centered culture. Ms. LEE expressed a preference to encourage public
  transit use and discussed enhancements to local ACT bus routes.

  Councilmember MALONEY further discussed the bus route on Valley Blvd., Alhambra’s work
  on the Bike and Pedestrian Plan, and his preference for reconsideration of BRT line through
  Alhambra. Mr. Roy CHOI answered questions. Mr. MALONEY and Mr. Roy CHOI also
  discussed long-term pedal assisted bike rental. Mr. Ricky CHOI stated that there would be
  other partnership opportunities to achieve a BRT line in Alhambra. Mr. Roy CHOI elaborated
  and clarified the difference between a rapid bus line and bus rapid transit (BRT) line. Mr.
  MALONEY went on to discuss the need for more accurate scheduling and arrival times at the
  bus route. Mr. MALONEY and Mr. Roy CHOI discussed the side travel versus curb running
  option.

  City Manager BINNQUIST clarified that the City had never taken a position against the BRT
  line at Valley Blvd. Assistant City Manager GARCIA further clarified the City’s inquiries into
  traffic on Valley Blvd. were in terms of development of the SR 710 stub and the proposed
  enhancements in the area. She clarified that it was not City staff’s intention to show any
  opposition or support of a BRT bus line on Valley Blvd. without evidence from the analysis.
  Mr. MALONEY acknowledged nature of the study and evidence presented.

  Vice Mayor PÉREZ expressed frustration with the SGVCOG Feasibility Study and the lack of
  coordination during the City development of its own Active Transportation Plan. Ms. PÉREZ
  stated that enhancements, such as the BRT line, were the types of opportunities the City
  sought in order to fully realize a more modern transportation plan for the City. Mr. Roy CHOI
  further clarified that while there was no opposition to the BRT line from City staff, that the
  decision to place a stop at Garvey Blvd. was supported by traffic studies, travel time metrics,
  ridership statistics, and was more aligned with the goal of the screening analysis to replace
  loss of services along the SR60 corridor per METRO. He reiterated that he was hopeful that
  given the long-term scope of the study that there might be future opportunities for the
  SGVCOG to seek new input from cities wherein the City of Alhambra could reiterate their
  desire for a BRT line at Valley Blvd. Mr. CHOI and Ms. PÉREZ continued to discuss the bus
  route at Valley Blvd.

  Ms. PÉREZ and Mr. Roy CHOI went on to briefly discuss potential long-term changes to the
  rail network running through Alhambra. Mr. CHOI stated that the project was unfunded at this
  time and Ms. PÉREZ expressed the City’s interest in developing those areas. Ms. PÉREZ, Mr.
  Roy CHOI, and Mr. Ricky CHOI continued to discuss the potential BRT line and the actions
  the City could take to work with Metro and the SGVCOG to further develop other aspects of
  the active transportation plan.

  Mayor MAZA thanked the SGVCOG representatives for their presentation, discussed the
  transportation outlook for the region, and echoed support for continued collaboration with the
  SGVCOG.
  3
2-26-24
   Action Taken:  City Council received and filed this informational report.

4.  2023 CITY ACCOMPLISHMENTS REPORT - F2M23-35

  Public Information Specialist Danielle RODRIGUEZ presented the 2023 Accomplishments
  Report which highlighted many of the past year’s achievements. The accomplishments
  aligned with the City’s Strategic Plan, which was prioritized to reflect the community’s core
  values. The Report was intended to heighten community awareness of new and ongoing
  activities and projects. The presentation and report are on file in the City Clerk’s office.

  Discussion: Council thanked City staff of each department for their continued hard work
  and expressed appreciation for the accomplishments in 2023.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the informational report.

5.  MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 AND RESOLUTION
  ADOPTING FY 2023-24 BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS – F2M23-17, R2M24-5

  Director of Finance Pearl LIEU delivered a staff report and presentation. The presentation is
  on file in the City Clerk’s office. On June 26, 2023, the City Council adopted the Budget for
  Fiscal Years 2023-24 and 2024-25, which appropriated funds and approved revenue
  projections for the fiscal year. During the fiscal year, unforeseen financial needs and
  opportunities typically arose, which required City Council approval of recommended
  adjustments to projected revenues and expenditures. Staff presented a mid-year Budget
  review to provide a Budget update for FY 2023-24. Ms. LIEU provided the City Council with a
  high-level overview of the FY 2022-23 actual performance and updated budget projections for
  FY 2023-24. Staff also requested that the City Council approve a resolution adopting the FY
  2023-24 Budget adjustments.

  Discussion: Council thanked Ms. Lieu and City staff for their work and praised the current
  surplus. Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. LIEU discussed the decreased State
  Gas Fund. Councilmember LEE and Ms. LIEU discussed the decreased sales tax revenue
  specifically from automobile dealers in Alhambra. Councilmember MALONEY and Ms. LIEU
  discussed the possibility of creating a staff position to oversee the implementation of the
  pending Sustainability Plan. Mr. MALONEY requested a presentation regarding the City’s
  investment funds at a future City Council meeting. Vice Mayor PÉREZ and City Attorney
  MONTES discussed the Opioid Settlement Fund.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the Mid-Year Budget Review and
  related reports; and, adopt Resolution No. R2M24-5 entitled: A Resolution of the Alhambra
  City Council adopting Fiscal Year 2023-24 Budget adjustments of the City of Alhambra, Golf
  Course Clubhouse Corporation, Alhambra Capital Improvements Corporation, Alhambra
  Parking Authority, Alhambra Facilities Financing Authority and the Alhambra Public Financing
  Authority

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

  4
2-26-24
 CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 6 – 31)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, except Item No. 30, were considered by the City Council
to be routine were enacted by one motion.

6.  ACCEPT SUMMER LUNCH PROGRAM GRANT FROM THE CALIFORNIA STATE
  LIBRARY AND APPROPRIATE FUNDS – F2M24-18, M2M24-28

  The California State Library offers grants in support of library programs and pop-up visits at
  summer lunch sites to enhance access to books and library services by the community. In
  November 2023, staff applied for this funding opportunity and was awarded $5,984 to support
  library programming at the City’s park sites participating under the free Summer Lunch
  Program. The grant funds would be used to purchase giveaway books and programming
  supplies to be used during the Library’s mobile visits this summer.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted $5,984 in grant funds from the California State
  Library to support the Library’s mobile summer programs and services; appropriate revenue
  and expenditure funds in the amount of $5,984; authorized the City Manager or designee to
  sign the grant agreement with the California State Library, subject to final language approval
  by the City Manager and City Attorney; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-28)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: 2024 USDA SUMMER FOOD SERVICE PROGRAM – F2M24-25,
  N2M24-27

  The Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) is a federally funded program administered by
  the State of California Department of Education. The proposed SFSP would begin distributing
  lunches and snacks on May 28, 2024 and would be provided Monday through Friday through
  August 2, 2024. Food would be distributed at Alhambra, Granada and Almansor Parks. The
  City would be eligible for reimbursement by the California Department of Education for
  lunches, snacks and operational costs.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the City’s participation in the 2024 Summer
  Food Service Program; authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to secure a vendor
  to provide prepared lunches and snacks for the program.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: ALMANSOR COURT EXTERIOR IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
  PHASE II – F2M24-26, N2M24-28

  5
2-26-24
   Specifications and bid documentation were completed for the Almansor Court Exterior
  Improvement Project Phase II. The project would include additional improvements to the
  exterior of the building, such as new doors to the Greenhouse room to match the new door in
  front of the building, new decorative lighted landscape bollards, repainting decorative lighting
  poles in front of the building, and repair of concrete path of travel areas surrounding the
  building. Bids would be due by 10:30 a.m. on April 11, 2024, in the office of the City Clerk and
  would be opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to
  prospective contractors for the Almansor Court Exterior Improvement Project Phase II; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL CONSULTING SERVICES TO ASSIST IN MANAGING
  THE IMPLEMENTATION PROGRAMS CONTAINED IN THE 2021-2029 HOUSING
  ELEMENT – F2M24-27, RPF2M24-4

  A required component of a jurisdiction’s Housing Element is a Housing Plan that must outline
  goals, programs, and policies to facilitate and encourage the development of housing in their
  community. Alhambra’s Housing Plan contained an Implementation Program with thirty
  separate programs that needed to be developed, monitored and tracked. In anticipation of the
  State certifying Alhambra’s Housing Element, staff sought to solicit proposals for a qualified
  firm to provide professional consulting services to assist the Planning Division in the oversight
  of the Housing Element to ensure that the Housing Element programs would be completed
  and within the timeframes identified.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the distribution of a Request for Proposals for
  professional consulting services to assist in managing the programs contained in the 2021-
  2029 Housing Element.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  AWARD CONTRACT: ALMANSOR GYMNASIUM WINDOW REPLACEMENT PROJECT –
  F2M23-77, N2M23-147, C2M24-11, M2M24-29

  On December 11, 2023, the City Council approved the distribution of Notice Inviting Bids for
  the Almansor Gymnasium Window Replacement Project. On January 25, 2024, the City Clerk
  received and opened five bids for the Project. The bids ranged from $115,000 (Dynasty
  Builders) to $755,760 (1st California Construction). Dynasty Builders Inc. submitted the lowest
  bid. However, during the bid evaluation process it was discovered that Dynasty Builders Inc.
  did not include Prevailing Wage, as required per the Notice Inviting Bids. Therefore, the bid
  from Dynasty Builders Inc. was deemed non-responsive. The second lower bidder First Trade
  6
2-26-24
   LLC (dba YMC) was deemed the lowest responsive bidder. Staff reviewed the bid submitted
  by First Trade LLC (dba YMC) and found it to be in full compliance and conformance with the
  project specifications.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and First Trade LLC
  (dba YMC) for the Almansor Gymnasium Window Replacement Project in an amount not to
  exceed $249,500.00; find the Project categorically exempt from California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15301; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-29)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

11.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: REHABLITATION OF THE STORM DRAIN PIPES ON
  COMMONWEALTH AVENUE AND GRAND AVENUE – F2M24-28, N2M24-29

  The storm drains located at the intersection of Commonwealth and Marguerita Avenues and
  at the intersection of Grand Avenue and 2nd Street were broken and collapsed causing a
  sinkhole. The storm drains needed to be repaired to handle normal water flow before flooding
  occurs and further damage ensues to the street. Plans and specifications were prepared. Staff
  reviewed the plans and found them to be consistent with City’s standards.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  qualified contractors for the Rehabilitation of the Storm Drain pipes on Commonwealth Avenue
  and Grand Avenue with bids due no later than 10:30 a.m. on March 21, 2024, and opened at
  11:00 a.m. that same day.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

12.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES FOR THE
  BURKE HERITAGE PARK AND MARENGO YARD STORMWATER CAPTURE PROJECT
  – F2M21-63, RFP2M24-5

  The Burke Heritage Park and Marengo Yard Stormwater Capture Project was identified as a
  priority concept in the Stormwater Master Plan. A feasibility study was completed in order to
  prepare the project for the design phase. The City received full funding for design and
  construction through the Safe Clean Water Regional Program. The project provided reduced
  stormwater runoff volumes and pollutant loads to receiving waters. The primary treatment best
  management practices (BMPs) would include dry wells, seasonal bioswale wetlands, and
  bioretention basins as well as Park and City facility improvements. In addition to the
  stormwater-related goals, the City pursued the Project with the added goals of maximizing
  community benefits under a Statewide Park Programs Grant and a State Grant Allocation

  7
2-26-24
   through Mike Fong for new recreation opportunities, increasing the tree canopy, enhancing
  park space, and designing the Project with community-based input.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the distribution of a Request for Proposals to
  qualified firms for Professional Engineering Design Services for the Burke Heritage Park and
  Marengo Yard Stormwater Capture Project.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

13.  RECORD A DEED RESTRICTION ON CITY PARK PROPERTY AT ALHAMBRA PARK IN
  ORDER TO COMPLY WITH MEASURE A GRANT REQUIREMENTS – F2M21-18, F2M22-
  66, F2M22-37, M2M24-30

  The City was eligible for Measure A grant funds which could be used for development projects
  that include construction, enhancement, or refurbishment of park or open space elements.
  These grants were administered by the Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space
  District (RPOSD) through various funding opportunities for which staff routinely apply for park
  improvement projects. At Alhambra Park, since 2022, staff executed two grants funded under
  Measure A: (1) Alhambra Park Restroom Renovations Project; and (2) Alhambra Park Pool
  Improvements. As a condition of the grants and in order to receive grant payments, the City
  must record a deed restriction on the properties where the grant-funded projects will be
  implemented. A deed restriction was required by the RPOSD to ensure that the properties are
  used for a purpose consistent with the grant scope and would remain as a public resource,
  per Measure A.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized recording a deed restriction on City park
  property at Alhambra Park in order to comply with the requirements under the Safe, Clean
  Neighborhood Parks, Open Space Beaches, Rivers Protection, and Water Conservation
  Measure (Measure A) grant program administered by the Los Angeles County Regional Park
  and Open Space District (RPOSD); and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-30)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

14.  RECORD A DEED RESTRICTION ON CITY PARK PROPERTY AT GRANADA PARK IN
  ORDER TO COMPLY WITH MEASURE A GRANT REQUIREMENTS – F2M21-18, M2M24-
  31

  The City was eligible for Measure A grant funds which could be used for development projects
  that include construction, enhancement, or refurbishment of park or open space elements.
  These grants were administered by the Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space
  District (RPOSD) through various funding opportunities for which staff routinely apply for park
  improvement projects. At Granada Park, staff executed a grant funded under Measure A for
  8
2-26-24
   new playground equipment and surfacing. As a condition of the grants and in order to receive
  grant payments, the City must record a deed restriction on the properties where the grant-
  funded projects will be implemented. A deed restriction was required by the RPOSD to ensure
  that the properties are used for a purpose consistent with the grant scope and would remain
  as a public resource, per Measure A.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized recording a deed restriction on City park
  property at Granada Park in order to comply with the requirements under the Safe, Clean
  Neighborhood Parks, Open Space Beaches, Rivers Protection, and Water Conservation
  Measure (Measure A) grant program administered by the Los Angeles County Regional Park
  and Open Space District (RPOSD); and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Councill’s action. (M2M24-31)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

15.  APPROVAL TO AMEND CONTRACT K2M23-381 WITH SAGECREST PLANNING AND
  ENVIRONMENTAL FOR TEMPORARY PLANNING STAFFING SERVICES – F2M24-16,
  K2M23-381, M2M24-32

  A promotion and resignation of two full-time Planners last year resulted in the Community
  Development Department needing to secure temporary contract Planners to maintain levels
  of service for the community and carry out the day-to-day functions of the Division. As a result,
  on December 5, 2023, the City entered into a contract with Sagecrest Planning and
  Environmental to provide temporary staffing services. The terms of contract K2M23-381 were
  such that services may not exceed $50,000. The original contract was envisioned to provide
  short-term staff support but the recruitment process has been longer than anticipated. To date,
  the contract reached its $50,000 limit and an additional $60,000 was necessary to allow
  contract Planners to wind down their projects and assist in the transition from temporary to
  permanent staffing.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract amendment, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and
  Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, for temporary planning staffing services for an amount
  not to exceed $110,000; authorized the transfer of appropriations from salaries to contract
  services to cover the excess costs; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize the Council’s action. (M2M24-32)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

16.  AWARD OF CONTRACT TO LEXISNEXIS – F2M24-29, C2M24-12, M2M24-33

  LexisNexis Desk Officer Reporting System (DORS) is a controlled-access online reporting
  system which community members can use to file reports, provide crime tips, and report other
  9
2-26-24
   incidents 24/7. It is a useful resource tool for handling a variety of incidents without the need
  for an officer on scene. Accurint Crime Analysis is another product from LexisNexis which is
  an online dashboard that enables crime data sharing, crime mapping and crime analytics. Both
  products directly interface with the Police Department’s Record Management System.
  LexisNexis is the sole source for DORS licenses, ongoing support and maintenance service.
  Sole source purchase is allowable under Alhambra Municipal Code Section 3.36.080(B)(2).
  Staff requested a five-year contract with an amount not to exceed $77,437.77.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to LexisNexis in the amount up to $77,437.77 for Desk
  Officer Reporting System (DORS) and Accurint Crime Analysis for a five-year period;
  authorized the City Manager to execute any additional documentation to extend the contract
  subject to satisfactory firm performance and future budget allocations; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-33)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

17.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: MAIN STREET SEWER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT
  BETWEEN GRANADA AVENUE AND EL MOLINO STREET – F2M23-26, C2M23-26,
  M2M24-34

  On April 24, 2023, the City Council awarded a contract to GRBCON, Inc. for the Main Street
  Sewer Main Replacement between Granada Avenue and El Molino Street in the amount of
  $710,879.00. There was one authorized change order during the project. The change order
  included the additional slurry seal, removing an abandoned sewer manhole lid and various

  TO ALLOW MEDICINAL CANNABIS DELIVERY-ONLY RETAILERS IN THE INDUSTRIAL
  ZONE WITH A CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT AND REGULATORY BUSINESS PERMIT TO
  IMPLEMENT THE REQUIREMENTS OF SB 1186 – F2M23-78, O2M24-4826

  15
2-26-24
   The California Legislature adopted Senate Bill 1886 (“SB 1186”) in 2022, entitled the Medicinal
  Cannabis Patients’ Right of Access Act, which precludes cities and counties from adopting or
  enforcing regulations that prohibit or have the effect of prohibiting the retail sale of medicinal
  cannabis by delivery. SB 1186 allowed cities and counties to adopt and enforce reasonable
  regulations on the retail sale by delivery of medicinal cannabis, including zoning requirements.
  The ordinance would allow a delivery-only retailer of medicinal cannabis to be a conditionally
  permitted use in the Industrial zone. The retailer must only sell medicinal cannabis; the retail
  sale of adult-use (e.g., recreational) cannabis would remain prohibited. As a delivery-only
  business, there would be no storefront operations (no walk-in customers). The ordinance also
  included separation requirements for such businesses. The ordinance also proposed that an
  annual business regulatory permit be required for such businesses. The ordinance included
  operational standards for these businesses. These included security requirements, odor
  control measures, and a requirement that product not be visible from the exterior of the
  property. Failure to comply with the operational requirements could result in the regulatory
  permit being suspended, revoked or not renewed.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council declared introduced for its second reading and adopt the
  following ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M24-4826: An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of
  Alhambra adopted pursuant to the City’s Police powers and Business
  Professions Code §26320 to amend Alhambra Municipal Code Section
  23.05.020 (Land Use Regulations – Commercial Zoning Districts), Section
  23.06.020 (Land Use Regulations – Employment Zoning Districts), and
  Section 23.22.080 (Cannabis Facilities, Cultivation, and Deliveries), to
  implement California law governing Medicinal Cannabis Delivery-Only
  retailers within the City
